title: Attention tiling and KV eviction explorations
content:
Goal:
- Capture experimental notes for CUDA tiling strategies paired with paged KV cache eviction/prefetch policies. Focused on improving end-to-end 1-2 token latency for long-context workloads while keeping cost per token low.

Background / motivation:
- FlashAttention (and variants) reduce memory footprint and improve throughput for attention but come with constraints: tiling shapes, register pressure, shared memory usage.
- Our paged KV cache (page-size ~64KB by default) trades off storage locality vs. host<->device transfer cost. Poor tiling + naive eviction leads to bursts of PCIe/NVLink transfers and tail latency spikes.
- Need heuristics that coordinate attention kernel tiling shapes with KV prefetch windows and eviction granularity.

High-level ideas tried so far (notes):
1) Two-tier tiling: small in-warp tile for compute, larger macro-tile for prefetching KV pages.
   - small tile: 16x64 (heads x seq tile) mapped to a CTA to maximize reuse in registers/shared memory.
   - macro-tile: 128 token chunk, aligns with our page boundaries to minimize partial-page fetches.
2) Eviction-by-age-and-cost: approximate LRU but bias eviction towards pages with low expected reuse (based on attention locality stats).
3) Prefetch window that is adaptive based on model temperature and seq-likelihood of touching future positions (heuristic from training logs).

Kernel-level notes (FlashAttention integration):
- We use FlashAttention style fused softmax + matmul to avoid storing full S matrix. This works best when the inner tile fits in shared memory. For our 16x64 tile, measured shared mem usage ~48KB / CTA on A100 which is high but acceptable if we restrict active CTAs to 2 per SM.
- Register pressure: Increasing tile width beyond 64 tokens pushes register spill and kills occupancy on GA100. Tradeoff point observed at ~96 tokens.
- Proposed change: micro-tiling inside the CTA: process 64-token steps in a loop, keep KV pages resident across loop iterations. This reduces page-churn since each CTA makes multiple passes over the same KV pages.

Bank conflicts and layout:
- KV pages currently laid out as [head-major][seq-major]. When we tile over seq-major chunks we observed bank conflicts on FP16 loads in shared memory on older Ampere cards. Experiment: transpose layout to [seq-major][head-major] in the hot path which reduced stall cycles by ~8% on T4 in our microbench.

KV paging heuristics and policies tested:
A) Fixed-page eviction: evict oldest page when memory cap reached. Simple but causes work-stealing of pages between concurrent requests.
B) Request-local pinning: pin pages that are actively used by a request until the request finishes. Avoids intra-request eviction but increases memory pressure.
C) Cost-aware eviction: maintain per-page score = alpha*age + beta*(estimated-transfer-cost) + gamma*(predicted-reuse). Choose knobs via small grid search.

Microbench results (representative):
- Baseline (no tiling coordination, fixed eviction): p95 latency for 4k context generative pass: 420ms; average throughput 18 tokens/s per GPU.
- With micro-tiling + request-local pinning: p95 = 320ms (24% drop), throughput = 22 tokens/s.
- With micro-tiling + cost-aware eviction + prefetch window=2 pages: p95 = 280ms, throughput = 26 tokens/s.
- Notes: p99 still spikes for sequences with random-access attention patterns (e.g., retrieval-augmented prompts).

Prefetch tuning details:
- Prefetch window measured in pages. Window=1 (prefetch next page) reduces stall events but increases PCIe bursts; window=2 smooths transfers. Window >3 has diminishing returns and increases memory footprint.
- Heuristic: if predicted token churn (new tokens referencing new pages) > 0.3, increase window to 2; else keep 1. Prediction is a cheap classifier over prompt metadata + recent attention distribution entropy.

Launch configuration and occupancy notes:
- Experimented with CTA size 256 threads (4 warps x 64 lanes) and 128 threads. 256 thread CTA increased shared memory pressure but allowed more cooperative loads using warp-wide intrinsics. 128 threads improved occupancy but required additional global memory passes.
- Kernel launch policy: choose CTA_size such that (shared_mem_per_CTA * CTAs_per_SM) <= shared_mem_SM_limit and registers_per_thread keeps registers_per_SM below threshold. We need a small autotuner on startup to pick per-model kernel params.

Observed tradeoffs / gotchas:
- Aligning macro-tiles to page boundaries is critical on NVLink clusters where remote access costs are high.
- On multi-tenant Dedicated instances, page eviction patterns of one tenant can cause IO storms for others (we need per-tenant quotas or separate pools).
- FlashAttention variants that fuse dropout/scale cause divergence with our quantized kernels (q4_0/q5). Workaround: run fused softmax in full fp16 path then quantized matmul separately; costs extra memory but preserves correctness.

Rough pseudocode for coordinated pipeline (simplified):
- for each request chunk:
    compute list of macro-tiles needed -> pages_to_touch
    pin pages_to_touch in local context (if memory budget allows)
    for macro_tile in macro_tiles:
       ensure pages resident (async prefetch if not)
       launch attention-CTA loop over micro-tiles inside macro_tile
    unpin pages

Open experiments / next steps (actionable):
- Add an in-kernel page residency counter visible to scheduler so we can avoid evicting a page that has >0 active CTAs.
- Implement lightweight per-request reuse estimator: collect attention entropy per request at runtime and feed into prefetch policy.
- Run longer p99 experiments with retrieval-augmented workloads (we suspect pathological patterns causing long-tail).
- Prototype a small autotuner that runs at model load time to pick tile dimensions (micro_tile x macro_tile) per device type.
- Evaluate effect of page-size doubling (128KB) on PCIe transfer efficiency vs memory fragmentation.

Questions / unresolved:
- How aggressive should cross-request pinning be in Dedicated environments? Need input from product on tenant isolation guarantees.
- Can we leverage HBM peer-to-peer hints to move pages between GPUs proactively for pinned multi-GPU requests?
- Is there appetite for making page-size configurable per-model (tradesoff fragmentation vs transfer overhead)?

References / logs:
- local perf traces: /logs/kv_paging/2025-01-23/* (shared folder)
- PR with initial prefetched-CTA changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Jira: RT-519 tracks KV paging redesign

Appendix: quick checklist before marking final:
- [ ] Add autotuner skeleton to model bootstrap path
- [ ] Stabilize cost-aware eviction weights (alpha/beta/gamma) via longer A/B tests
- [ ] Add per-tenant memory accounting and throttle prefetch when quota exceeded

Notes-to-self: keep micro-tiling conservative on older Turing GPUs (lower register file) — fallback tiling profile is necessary.

-- Aisha
